method.renderer: Production write_latex_pdf with extended convergent compilation; instrumentation only adds LuaTeX status log lines every 100 pages and at end of document.
method.timed_scope: Complete write_latex_pdf call including rendering, media copying, and all convergent LuaLaTeX passes; synthetic snapshot/model/media preparation and PDF audit excluded.
method.rss_sampling: One-second ps samples of LuaLaTeX/LuaHBTeX processes during the renderer call; page memory checkpoints are associated with the current compiler pass.
method.comparison: Diagnostic media ablation; the no-media PDF is intentionally not semantically equivalent to the media fixture.

comparison_to_media_profile.purpose: Diagnostic estimate of media contribution; the no-media PDF is intentionally not semantically equivalent to the media fixture.
interpretation: One run per fixture does not establish a stable causal effect.
Removing 200 media records and 400 accessible figures reduced the page count by 218, but the sampled peak RSS was only 11.12 MiB lower.
The no-media run still reached 1140.77 MiB RSS, so media do not appear to be the main source of the peak in this fixture.

The Lua heap counter was about 52 MiB lower at the end of the final tagged pass, while peak RSS changed much less; these are distinct measurements and should not be treated as a byte-for-byte decomposition.

The media run first pass had a 266.81-MiB RSS peak while tagging was off and Hyperref was in draft mode; later tagged passes peaked at 1151.89 MiB. This points to the full tagged-link/PDF-management path for inspection, but that pass changes both tagging and Hyperref and is not an isolated causal test.
